lines.speaker: Mistress Quickly
lines.text: A kind heart he hath; a woman would run through fire and water for

lines.speaker: Mistress Quickly
lines.text: such a kind heart. But yet I would my master had Mistress Anne; or

lines.speaker: Mistress Quickly
lines.text: I would Master Slender had her; or, in sooth, I would Master Fenton

lines.speaker: Mistress Quickly
lines.text: had her; I will do what I can for them all three, for so I have

lines.speaker: Mistress Quickly
lines.text: promised, and I'll be as good as my word; but speciously for Master

lines.speaker: Mistress Quickly
lines.text: Fenton. Well, I must of another errand to Sir John Falstaff from my

lines.speaker: Mistress Quickly
lines.text: two mistresses: what a beast am I to slack it!

scenes.setting: A room in the Garter Inn.

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: Bardolph, I say,--

lines.speaker: Bardolph
lines.text: Here, sir.

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: Go fetch me a quart of sack; put a toast in 't.

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: Have I lived to be carried in a basket, and to be thrown in the

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: Thames like a barrow of butcher's offal? Well, if I be served such

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: another trick, I'll have my brains ta'en out and buttered, and give

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: them to a dog for a new year's gift. The rogues slighted me into

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: the river with as little remorse as they would have drowned a blind

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: bitch's puppies, fifteen i' the litter; and you may know by my size

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: that I have a kind of alacrity in sinking; if the bottom were as

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: deep as hell I should down. I had been drowned but that the shore

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: was shelvy and shallow; a death that I abhor, for the water swells

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: a man; and what a thing should I have been when had been swelled!

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: I should have been a mountain of mummy.

lines.speaker: Bardolph
lines.text: Here's Mistress Quickly, sir, to speak with you.

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: Come, let me pour in some sack to the Thames water; for my belly's

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: as cold as if I had swallowed snowballs for pills to cool the reins.

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: Call her in.

lines.speaker: Bardolph
lines.text: Come in, woman.

lines.speaker: Mistress Quickly
lines.text: By your leave. I cry you mercy. Give your worship good morrow.

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: Take away these chalices. Go, brew me a pottle of sack finely.

lines.speaker: Bardolph
lines.text: With eggs, sir?

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: Simple of itself; I'll no pullet-sperm in my brewage.

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: How now!

lines.speaker: Mistress Quickly
lines.text: Marry, sir, I come to your worship from Mistress Ford.

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: Mistress Ford! I have had ford enough; I was thrown into the ford;

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: I have my belly full of ford.

lines.speaker: Mistress Quickly
lines.text: Alas the day! good heart, that was not her fault: she does so take

lines.speaker: Mistress Quickly
lines.text: on with her men; they mistook their erection.

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: So did I mine, to build upon a foolish woman's promise.

lines.speaker: Mistress Quickly
lines.text: Well, she laments, sir, for it, that it would yearn your heart to

lines.speaker: Mistress Quickly
lines.text: see it. Her husband goes this morning a-birding; she desires you

lines.speaker: Mistress Quickly
lines.text: once more to come to her between eight and nine; I must carry her

lines.speaker: Mistress Quickly
lines.text: word quickly. She'll make you amends, I warrant you.

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: Well, I will visit her. Tell her so; and bid her think what a man

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: is; let her consider his frailty, and then judge of my merit.

lines.speaker: Mistress Quickly
lines.text: I will tell her.

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: Do so. Between nine and ten, sayest thou?

lines.speaker: Mistress Quickly
lines.text: Eight and nine, sir.

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: Well, be gone; I will not miss her.

lines.speaker: Mistress Quickly
lines.text: Peace be with you, sir.

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: I marvel I hear not of Master Brook; he sent me word to stay within.

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: I like his money well. O! here he comes.

lines.speaker: Ford
lines.text: Bless you, sir!

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: Now, Master Brook, you come to know what hath passed between me

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: and Ford's wife?

lines.speaker: Ford
lines.text: That, indeed, Sir John, is my business.

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: Master Brook, I will not lie to you: I was at her house the hour

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: she appointed me.

lines.speaker: Ford
lines.text: And how sped you, sir?

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: Very ill-favouredly, Master Brook.

lines.speaker: Ford
lines.text: How so, sir? did she change her determination?

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: No. Master Brook; but the peaking cornuto her husband, Master Brook,

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: dwelling in a continual 'larum of jealousy, comes me in the instant

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: of our encounter, after we had embraced, kissed, protested, and, as

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: it were, spoke the prologue of our comedy; and at his heels a

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: rabble of his companions, thither provoked and instigated by his

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: distemper, and, forsooth, to search his house for his wife's love.

lines.speaker: Ford
lines.text: What! while you were there?

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: While I was there.

lines.speaker: Ford
lines.text: And did he search for you, and could not find you?

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: You shall hear. As good luck would have it, comes in one Mistress

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: Page; gives intelligence of Ford's approach; and, in her invention

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: and Ford's wife's distraction, they conveyed me into a buck-basket.

lines.speaker: Ford
lines.text: A buck-basket!

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: By the Lord, a buck-basket! rammed me in with foul shirts and

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: smocks, socks, foul stockings, greasy napkins, that, Master Brook,

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: there was the rankest compound of villainous smell that ever

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: offended nostril.

lines.speaker: Ford
lines.text: And how long lay you there?

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: Nay, you shall hear, Master Brook, what I have suffered to bring

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: this woman to evil for your good. Being thus crammed in the basket,

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: a couple of Ford's knaves, his hinds, were called forth by their

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: mistress to carry me in the name of foul clothes to Datchet-lane;

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: they took me on their shoulders; met the jealous knave their

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: master in the door; who asked them once or twice what they had in

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: their basket. I quaked for fear lest the lunatic knave would have

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: searched it; but Fate, ordaining he should be a cuckold, held his

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: hand. Well, on went he for a search, and away went I for foul

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: clothes. But mark the sequel, Master Brook: I suffered the pangs

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: of three several deaths: first, an intolerable fright to be

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: detected with a jealous rotten bell-wether; next, to be compassed

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: like a good bilbo in the circumference of a peck, hilt to

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: point, heel to head; and then, to be stopped in, like a strong

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: distillation, with stinking clothes that fretted in their own

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: grease: think of that; a man of my kidney, think of that, that am

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: as subject to heat as butter; a man of continual dissolution and

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: thaw: it was a miracle to 'scape suffocation. And in the height

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: of this bath, when I was more than half stewed in grease, like

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: a Dutch dish, to be thrown into the Thames, and cooled, glowing

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: hot, in that surge, like a horse-shoe; think of that, hissing hot,

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: think of that, Master Brook!

lines.speaker: Ford
lines.text: In good sadness, sir, I am sorry that for my sake you have suffered

lines.speaker: Ford
lines.text: all this. My suit, then, is desperate; you'll undertake her no more.

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: Master Brook, I will be thrown into Etna, as I have been into

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: Thames, ere I will leave her thus. Her husband is this morning

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: gone a-birding; I have received from her another embassy of

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: meeting; 'twixt eight and nine is the hour, Master Brook.

lines.speaker: Ford
lines.text: 'Tis past eight already, sir.

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: Is it? I will then address me to my appointment. Come to me at

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: your convenient leisure, and you shall know how I speed, and the

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: conclusion shall be crowned with your enjoying her: adieu. You

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: shall have her, Master Brook; Master Brook, you shall cuckold Ford.

lines.speaker: Ford
lines.text: Hum! ha! Is this a vision? Is this a dream? Do I sleep? Master Ford,

lines.speaker: Ford
lines.text: awake; awake, Master Ford. There's a hole made in your best coat,

lines.speaker: Ford
lines.text: Master Ford. This 'tis to be married; this 'tis to have linen and

lines.speaker: Ford
lines.text: buck-baskets! Well, I will proclaim myself what I am; I will now

lines.speaker: Ford
lines.text: take the lecher; he is at my house. He cannot scape me; 'tis

lines.speaker: Ford
lines.text: impossible he should; he cannot creep into a half-penny purse, nor

lines.speaker: Ford
lines.text: into a pepper box; but, lest the devil that guides him should aid

lines.speaker: Ford
lines.text: him, I will search impossible places. Though what I am I cannot

lines.speaker: Ford
lines.text: avoid, yet to be what I would not, shall not make me tame; if I

lines.speaker: Ford
lines.text: have horns to make one mad, let the proverb go with me; I'll be

lines.speaker: Ford
lines.text: horn-mad.

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: Is he at Master Ford's already, think'st thou?

lines.speaker: Mistress Quickly
lines.text: Sure he is by this; or will be presently; but truly he is very

lines.speaker: Mistress Quickly
lines.text: courageous mad about his throwing into the water. Mistress Ford

lines.speaker: Mistress Quickly
lines.text: desires you to come suddenly.

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: I'll be with her by and by; I'll but bring my young man here to

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: school. Look where his master comes; 'tis a playing day, I see.

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: How now, Sir Hugh, no school to-day?

lines.speaker: Sir Hugh Evans
lines.text: No; Master Slender is let the boys leave to play.

lines.speaker: Mistress Quickly
lines.text: Blessing of his heart!

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: Sir Hugh, my husband says my son profits nothing in the world at

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: his book; I pray you ask him some questions in his accidence.

lines.speaker: Sir Hugh Evans
lines.text: Come hither, William; hold up your head; come.

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: Come on, sirrah; hold up your head; answer your master; be not afraid.

lines.text: William, how many numbers is in nouns?

lines.speaker: William Page
lines.text: Two.

lines.speaker: Mistress Quickly
lines.text: Truly, I thought there had been one number more, because they say

lines.speaker: Mistress Quickly
lines.text: 'Od's nouns.'

lines.speaker: Sir Hugh Evans
lines.text: Peace your tattlings! What is 'fair,' William?

lines.speaker: William Page
lines.text: Pulcher.

lines.speaker: Mistress Quickly
lines.text: Polecats! There are fairer things than polecats, sure.

lines.speaker: Sir Hugh Evans
lines.text: You are a very simplicity 'oman; I pray you, peace. What is

lines.speaker: Sir Hugh Evans
lines.text: 'lapis,' William?

lines.speaker: William Page
lines.text: A stone.

lines.speaker: Sir Hugh Evans
lines.text: And what is 'a stone,' William?

lines.speaker: William Page
lines.text: A pebble.

lines.speaker: Sir Hugh Evans
lines.text: No, it is 'lapis'; I pray you remember in your prain.

lines.speaker: William Page
lines.text: Lapis.

lines.speaker: Sir Hugh Evans
lines.text: That is a good William. What is he, William, that does lend articles?

lines.speaker: William Page
lines.text: Articles are borrowed of the pronoun, and be thus declined:

lines.speaker: William Page
lines.text: Singulariter, nominativo; hic, haec, hoc.

lines.speaker: Sir Hugh Evans
lines.text: Nominativo, hig, hag, hog; pray you, mark: genitivo, hujus. Well,

lines.speaker: Sir Hugh Evans
lines.text: what is your accusative case?

lines.speaker: William Page
lines.text: Accusativo, hinc.

lines.speaker: Sir Hugh Evans
lines.text: I pray you, have your remembrance, child. Accusativo, hung, hang, hog.

lines.speaker: Mistress Quickly
lines.text: 'Hang-hog' is Latin for bacon, I warrant you.

lines.speaker: Sir Hugh Evans
lines.text: Leave your prabbles, 'oman. What is the focative case, William?

lines.speaker: William Page
lines.text: O vocativo, O.

lines.speaker: Sir Hugh Evans
lines.text: Remember, William: focative is caret.

lines.speaker: Mistress Quickly
lines.text: And that's a good root.

lines.speaker: Sir Hugh Evans
lines.text: 'Oman, forbear.

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: Peace.

lines.speaker: Sir Hugh Evans
lines.text: What is your genitive case plural, William?

lines.speaker: William Page
lines.text: Genitive case?

lines.speaker: Sir Hugh Evans
lines.text: Ay.

lines.speaker: William Page
lines.text: Genitive: horum, harum, horum.

lines.speaker: Mistress Quickly
lines.text: Vengeance of Jenny's case; fie on her! Never name her, child, if

lines.speaker: Mistress Quickly
lines.text: she be a whore.

lines.speaker: Sir Hugh Evans
lines.text: For shame, 'oman.

lines.speaker: Mistress Quickly
lines.text: You do ill to teach the child such words. He teaches him to hick

lines.speaker: Mistress Quickly
lines.text: and to hack, which they'll do fast enough of themselves; and to

lines.speaker: Mistress Quickly
lines.text: call 'horum;' fie upon you!

lines.speaker: Sir Hugh Evans
lines.text: 'Oman, art thou lunatics? Hast thou no understandings for thy cases,

lines.speaker: Sir Hugh Evans
lines.text: and the numbers of the genders? Thou art as foolish Christian

lines.speaker: Sir Hugh Evans
lines.text: creatures as I would desires.

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: Prithee, hold thy peace.

lines.speaker: Sir Hugh Evans
lines.text: Show me now, William, some declensions of your pronouns.

lines.speaker: William Page
lines.text: Forsooth, I have forgot.

lines.speaker: Sir Hugh Evans
lines.text: It is qui, quae, quod; if you forget your 'quis', your 'quaes',

lines.speaker: Sir Hugh Evans
lines.text: and your 'quods', you must be preeches. Go your ways and play; go.

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: He is a better scholar than I thought he was.

lines.speaker: Sir Hugh Evans
lines.text: He is a good sprag memory. Farewell, Mistress Page.

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: Adieu, good Sir Hugh.

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: Get you home, boy. Come, we stay too long.

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: Mistress Ford, your sorrow hath eaten up my sufferance. I see you

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: are obsequious in your love, and I profess requital to a hair's

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: breadth; not only, Mistress Ford, in the simple office of love,

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: but in all the accoutrement, complement, and ceremony of it. But

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: are you sure of your husband now?

lines.speaker: Mistress Ford
lines.text: He's a-birding, sweet Sir John.

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: What ho! gossip Ford, what ho!

lines.speaker: Mistress Ford
lines.text: Step into the chamber, Sir John.

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: How now, sweetheart! who's at home besides yourself?

lines.speaker: Mistress Ford
lines.text: Why, none but mine own people.

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: Indeed!

lines.speaker: Mistress Ford
lines.text: No, certainly.--

lines.speaker: Mistress Ford
lines.text: Speak louder.

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: Truly, I am so glad you have nobody here.

lines.speaker: Mistress Ford
lines.text: Why?

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: Why, woman, your husband is in his old lunes again. He so takes

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: on yonder with my husband; so rails against all married mankind;

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: so curses all Eve's daughters, of what complexion soever; and so

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: buffets himself on the forehead, crying 'Peer out, peer out!'

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: that any madness I ever yet beheld seemed but tameness, civility,

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: and patience, to this his distemper he is in now. I am glad the

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: fat knight is not here.

lines.speaker: Mistress Ford
lines.text: Why, does he talk of him?

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: Of none but him; and swears he was carried out, the last time he

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: searched for him, in a basket; protests to my husband he is now

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: here; and hath drawn him and the rest of their company from their

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: sport, to make another experiment of his suspicion. But I am glad

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: the knight is not here; now he shall see his own foolery.

lines.speaker: Mistress Ford
lines.text: How near is he, Mistress Page?

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: Hard by, at street end; he will be here anon.

lines.speaker: Mistress Ford
lines.text: I am undone! the knight is here.

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: Why, then, you are utterly shamed, and he's but a dead man. What

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: a woman are you! Away with him, away with him! better shame than

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: murder.

lines.speaker: Mistress Ford
lines.text: Which way should he go? How should I bestow him? Shall I put him

lines.speaker: Mistress Ford
lines.text: into the basket again?

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: No, I'll come no more i' the basket. May I not go out ere he come?

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: Alas! three of Master Ford's brothers watch the door with pistols,

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: that none shall issue out; otherwise you might slip away ere he

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: came. But what make you here?

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: What shall I do? I'll creep up into the chimney.

lines.speaker: Mistress Ford
lines.text: There they always use to discharge their birding-pieces.

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: Creep into the kiln-hole.

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: Where is it?

lines.speaker: Mistress Ford
lines.text: He will seek there, on my word. Neither press, coffer, chest, trunk,

lines.speaker: Mistress Ford
lines.text: well, vault, but he hath an abstract for the remembrance of such

lines.speaker: Mistress Ford
lines.text: places, and goes to them by his note: there is no hiding you in

lines.speaker: Mistress Ford
lines.text: the house.

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: I'll go out then.

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: If you go out in your own semblance, you die, Sir John. Unless

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: you go out disguised,--

lines.speaker: Mistress Ford
lines.text: How might we disguise him?

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: Alas the day! I know not! There is no woman's gown big enough for

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: him; otherwise he might put on a hat, a muffler, and a kerchief,

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: and so escape.

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: Good hearts, devise something: any extremity rather than a mischief.

lines.speaker: Mistress Ford
lines.text: My maid's aunt, the fat woman of Brainford, has a gown above.

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: On my word, it will serve him; she's as big as he is; and there's

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: her thrummed hat, and her muffler too. Run up, Sir John.

lines.speaker: Mistress Ford
lines.text: Go, go, sweet Sir John. Mistress Page and I will look some linen

lines.speaker: Mistress Ford
lines.text: for your head.

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: Quick, quick! we'll come dress you straight; put on the gown the while.

lines.speaker: Mistress Ford
lines.text: I would my husband would meet him in this shape; he cannot abide

lines.speaker: Mistress Ford
lines.text: the old woman of Brainford; he swears she's a witch, forbade her

lines.speaker: Mistress Ford
lines.text: my house, and hath threatened to beat her.

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: Heaven guide him to thy husband's cudgel; and the devil guide his

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: cudgel afterwards!

lines.speaker: Mistress Ford
lines.text: But is my husband coming?

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: Ay, in good sadness is he; and talks of the basket too, howsoever

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: he hath had intelligence.

lines.speaker: Mistress Ford
lines.text: We'll try that; for I'll appoint my men to carry the basket again,

lines.speaker: Mistress Ford
lines.text: to meet him at the door with it as they did last time.

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: Nay, but he'll be here presently; let's go dress him like the

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: witch of Brainford.

lines.speaker: Mistress Ford
lines.text: I'll first direct my men what they shall do with the basket. Go up;

lines.speaker: Mistress Ford
lines.text: I'll bring linen for him straight.

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: Hang him, dishonest varlet! we cannot misuse him enough.

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: We'll leave a proof, by that which we will do,

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: Wives may be merry and yet honest too.

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: We do not act that often jest and laugh;

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: 'Tis old but true: 'Still swine eats all the draff.'

lines.text: Come, come, take it up.

lines.text: Ay, but if it prove true, Master Page, have you any way then to

lines.text: unfool me again? Set down the basket, villain! Somebody call my

lines.text: wife. Youth in a basket! O you panderly rascals! there's a knot,

lines.text: a ging, a pack, a conspiracy against me. Now shall the devil be

lines.text: I went to her in white and cried 'mum' and she cried 'budget'

lines.speaker: Slender
lines.text: as Anne and I had appointed; and yet it was not Anne, but a

lines.speaker: Slender
lines.text: postmaster's boy.

lines.speaker: Sir Hugh Evans
lines.text: Jeshu! Master Slender, cannot you see put marry poys?

lines.speaker: Page
lines.text: O I am vexed at heart: what shall I do?

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: Good George, be not angry: I knew of your purpose; turned my

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: daughter into green; and, indeed, she is now with the doctor at

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: the deanery, and there married.

lines.speaker: Doctor Caius
lines.text: Vere is Mistress Page? By gar, I am cozened; I ha' married un

lines.speaker: Doctor Caius
lines.text: garcon, a boy; un paysan, by gar, a boy; it is not Anne Page;

lines.speaker: Doctor Caius
lines.text: by gar, I am cozened.

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: Why, did you take her in green?

lines.speaker: Doctor Caius
lines.text: Ay, by gar, and 'tis a boy: by gar, I'll raise all Windsor.

lines.speaker: Ford
lines.text: This is strange. Who hath got the right Anne?

lines.speaker: Page
lines.text: My heart misgives me; here comes Master Fenton.

lines.speaker: Page
lines.text: How now, Master Fenton!

lines.speaker: Anne Page
lines.text: Pardon, good father! good my mother, pardon!

lines.speaker: Page
lines.text: Now, Mistress, how chance you went not with Master Slender?

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: Why went you not with Master Doctor, maid?

lines.speaker: Fenton
lines.text: You do amaze her: hear the truth of it.

lines.speaker: Fenton
lines.text: You would have married her most shamefully,

lines.speaker: Fenton
lines.text: Where there was no proportion held in love.

lines.speaker: Fenton
lines.text: The truth is, she and I, long since contracted,

lines.speaker: Fenton
lines.text: Are now so sure that nothing can dissolve us.

lines.speaker: Fenton
lines.text: The offence is holy that she hath committed,

lines.speaker: Fenton
lines.text: And this deceit loses the name of craft,

lines.speaker: Fenton
lines.text: Of disobedience, or unduteous title,

lines.speaker: Fenton
lines.text: Since therein she doth evitate and shun

lines.speaker: Fenton
lines.text: A thousand irreligious cursed hours,

lines.speaker: Fenton
lines.text: Which forced marriage would have brought upon her.

lines.speaker: Ford
lines.text: Stand not amaz'd: here is no remedy:

lines.speaker: Ford
lines.text: In love, the heavens themselves do guide the state:

lines.speaker: Ford
lines.text: Money buys lands, and wives are sold by fate.

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: I am glad, though you have ta'en a special stand

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: to strike at me, that your arrow hath glanced.

lines.speaker: Page
lines.text: Well, what remedy?--Fenton, heaven give thee joy!

lines.speaker: Page
lines.text: What cannot be eschew'd must be embrac'd.

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: When night-dogs run, all sorts of deer are chas'd.

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: Well, I will muse no further. Master Fenton,

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: Heaven give you many, many merry days!

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: Good husband, let us every one go home,

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: And laugh this sport o'er by a country fire;

lines.speaker: Mistress Page
lines.text: Sir John and all.

lines.speaker: Ford
lines.text: Let it be so. Sir John,

lines.speaker: Ford
lines.text: To Master Brook you yet shall hold your word;

lines.speaker: Ford
lines.text: For he, to-night, shall lie with Mistress Ford.
